samples.summary: Hybrid snapshot/live model: paste now reads the merge layout live while the cell grid stays a copy-time snapshot, so the two can disagree
samples.evidence: `copy`/`cut` snapshot `grid`, `rangeStyles`, `sourceRange` and `text`, but `paste` now derives `copiedMerges` from `this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` at paste time. The two halves of the same copy operation are therefore taken at different points in time. If the user merges cells inside the source range *after* copying, the paste re-creates a block that was never part of the copied content and `clearCellsUnderMerge` then deletes destination cells the (uncopied) block hides; conversely a copied value now covered at the source is still written from the stale grid and then cleared. The design doc rewrite (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:98-104) asserts merges are read live "never a copy-time snapshot" without reconciling that the grid it pairs them with *is* a copy-time snapshot, so the documented model is internally inconsistent with the implementation's other half.

samples.summary: Root cause (a copy buffer that survives structural mutation) is only half-addressed: sourceRange/grid are never invalidated by shiftCells/moveRows/moveColumns
samples.evidence: The new comment at sheet.ts:2201-2203 names the real defect: "a snapshot survives `shiftCells`, `moveRows`/`moveColumns` and `unmergeSelection`". The fix only re-reads *merges* live; `this.copyBuffer.sourceRange` and `.grid` are still the stale pre-shift snapshot, and `clearCopyBuffer()` is called only from the two view layers (worksheet.ts:4902, worksheet.ts:5074, spreadsheet.ts:718) — never from any row/column mutation in sheet.ts. After `insertRows`/`moveRows`, an internal paste still computes deltaRow/deltaCol and `getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` against coordinates that no longer describe the copied cells, so the live read is aimed at the wrong region. Invalidating (or shifting) the copy buffer on structural mutation is the layer where this belongs.
searchedFor: grep shiftCells/moveRows call sites in sheet.ts

samples.summary: The new boolean conflates "refused" with "nothing to paste", so pivot sheets and empty clipboards now pin the copy buffer open
samples.evidence: `paste` returns `false` for a pivot sheet (line 2173), for no text/html (2247) and for an empty grid (2254), as well as for a merge refusal. Both callers (worksheet.ts:4901, spreadsheet.ts:717) only call `clearCopyBuffer()` on `true`, so pasting into a pivot sheet or with an empty clipboard now silently keeps the marching ants and buffer alive, which is not the behaviour the doc paragraph (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:109) promises ("a rejection leaves the copy buffer ... intact"). A distinct refusal signal (or clearing the buffer for the not-applicable cases) would express the intended contract.

samples.summary: For HTML/TSV pastes the overwrite check uses the grid bounding box, which can under-report the pasted area and refuse a paste that would in fact fully cover the block
samples.evidence: `pasteRange = rangeOf(grid)` shrinks to the non-empty cells only (`html2grid` drops empty cells, per the new comment at 2274-2277). A pasted region whose outer cells are empty therefore yields a bounding box narrower than the visual paste area, so a merged block that the user's paste area fully covers can be classified as "only partially overwritten" and the whole paste rejected. The internal-paste branch avoids this by carrying an explicit translated `pasteRange`; the external branches have no equivalent notion of the true paste extent.

finding.summary: Hybrid snapshot/live model: paste now reads the merge layout live while the cell grid stays a copy-time snapshot, so the two can disagree
finding.evidence: `copy`/`cut` snapshot `grid`, `rangeStyles`, `sourceRange` and `text`, but `paste` now derives `copiedMerges` from `this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` at paste time. The two halves of the same copy operation are therefore taken at different points in time. If the user merges cells inside the source range *after* copying, the paste re-creates a block that was never part of the copied content and `clearCellsUnderMerge` then deletes destination cells the (uncopied) block hides; conversely a copied value now covered at the source is still written from the stale grid and then cleared. The design doc rewrite (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:98-104) asserts merges are read live "never a copy-time snapshot" without reconciling that the grid it pairs them with *is* a copy-time snapshot, so the documented model is internally inconsistent with the implementation's other half.

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree: `copy`/`cut` snapshot the grid, rangeStyles, sourceRange and text into `copyBuffer` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2133-2153), while the internal-paste branch relocates that snapshot (2195-2199) yet derives `copiedMerges` from a LIVE `this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` call at paste time (2204), with an in-code comment stating the live read is deliberate. The resulting `pastedMerges` are re-created at the destination and `clearCellsUnderMerge` (2336-2344, implementation 918-948) deletes destination cells the new block hides — including cells just written from the stale snapshot by `setGrid` (2295). The hybrid temporal model is therefore exactly as described. It is reachable: `copyBuffer` is never invalidated by model mutations — `clearCopyBuffer` is only invoked from view code after a successful paste (view/worksheet.ts:4902), on Escape (view/worksheet.ts:5074) and spreadsheet.ts:718 — and neither `mergeSelection` (4439-4468) nor `unmergeSelection` (4493-4521) clears it; merging also does not change the system clipboard text, so the `text === copyBuffer.text` internal-paste branch still fires after a post-copy merge. The design doc claim is also accurate: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:97-110 asserts merges are read live "never a copy-time snapshot" while the surrounding copy/paste description (92-96) rests on the snapshotting buffer, and the tension is never reconciled. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable, and the finding is a data-model/abstraction-coherence claim rather than a pure line-level bug, so I cannot call it out-of-scope with confidence.

verdict.reason: The absence is factually real — I confirmed clearCopyBuffer's only call sites are the two post-paste handlers and Escape (view/worksheet.ts:4902, 5074; view/spreadsheet.ts:718), and that shiftCells (sheet.ts:1277-1364) / moveCells (sheet.ts:1449-1500) shift dimensions, rangeStyles, conditionalFormats, dataValidations, merges and filter state but never this.copyBuffer (only assignments: sheet.ts:2125, 2138, 2151, 2291). However it is not blocking under the design-fit/spec-conformance rubric. (1) The originating spec, docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheet-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md, scopes the work to carrying merge metadata through copy/cut-paste; all its Todo/Approach items are implemented (live merge read + propagate-or-reject at sheet.ts:2200-2231 and 2262-2288), and copy-buffer invalidation on structural mutation is in neither its acceptance items nor its Non-goals — the finding names no criterion it fails. (2) The live-read approach is the documented design, not an undocumented gap: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:98-100 states paste reads copied blocks from the live sheet "never a copy-time snapshot, which row/column shifts and unmergeSelection would invalidate". Preferring buffer invalidation instead is a design preference (minor, never blocking). (3) The concrete harm described — deltaRow/deltaCol and getMergesIntersecting aimed at stale coordinates after insertRows/moveRows — is a stale-coordinate logic bug and a pre-existing, merge-independent property of the copyBuffer snapshot (sheet.ts:2138/2151), i.e. the correctness lens's lane, which this rubric explicitly defers.

finding.summary: New private `gridRange` reinvents the existing exported helper `rangeOf(grid): Range` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18), which already computes a grid's bounding box in the same package. The repo expects reuse of the shared coordinate helpers; the only semantic difference is the empty-grid contract (`rangeOf` returns an Infinity range instead of `undefined`), which could have been handled by extending or wrapping `rangeOf` rather than adding a second bounding-box implementation inside the Sheet class. The todo doc even bills this as an "extract and reuse" step, but the extraction landed as a class-private duplicate instead of the existing utility.
finding.evidence: coordinates.ts:18 `export function rangeOf(grid: Grid): Range` vs sheet.ts:2391 `private gridRange(grid: Grid): Range | undefined`

verdict.reason: The finding asserts a private duplicate bounding-box method `private gridRange(grid: Grid): Range | undefined` at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2391. That code is not present. A repo-wide grep for `gridRange` matches only prose in docs/tasks/active/20260822-sheet-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:50,58 and prior reviewer artifacts under .agent-review/ — no such method exists in packages/sheets/src. The real sheet.ts:2384-2405 `selectPastedRange` REUSES the shared helper: it imports `rangeOf` at sheet.ts:9 and destructures `rangeOf(grid)` at sheet.ts:2389, with the empty-grid contract handled by the early return `if (grid.size === 0) return;` at sheet.ts:2388 — i.e. exactly the wrap-rather-than-duplicate approach the finding demands. The other paste path also reuses it at sheet.ts:2255 (`pasteRange = pasteRange ?? rangeOf(grid)`). `rangeOf` at coordinates.ts:18 is the sole bounding-box implementation; a scan of Math.min/Math.max in sheet.ts finds no grid-key bounding-box recomputation. Only a stale name in the todo doc remains, which is a wording nit, not a duplication/reuse violation.
